contexts.text: That Jonah was in the viscera of the fish three days and three nights, manifestly represented the burial and resurrection of the Lord on the third day.
The particulars in Jonah concerning Nineveh... are historical, yet are prophetical.
The Lord's temptations against the Hells are thus prophetically described by Jonah when he was in the belly of the great fish.
This is historically true, but still was representative; as is everything historical of the Word in the book... of Jonah, etc.

There are also like things in the world; for all these things come forth actually on earth; so that it cannot be otherwise than that they should come forth, seeing they are significative; as that Jonah was swallowed by a whale, which actually took place in the world...

That by Jonah being three days and three nights in the whale was represented that the Lord should be so in the heart of the earth, He Himself teaches... And by these words of Jonah () are described the direful temptations of the Lord...

That Jonah was in the belly of the whale three days and three nights, and that this was taken as a sign, was because it signified the burial and resurrection of the Lord, thus the glorification of His Human to the full.
